title: Cookbook:Acid Drops
text: Bring the sugar, water and cream of tartar to boil over medium-low heat.

title: Cookbook:Acid Drops
text: Stir gently until syrup reaches 310°F (155°C/hard crack stage) or is pale brown.

title: Cookbook:Acid Drops
text: Syrup should harden completely when dropped on to a cold plate and snap between the teeth when cold.

title: Cookbook:Acid Drops
text: Pour the mixture onto an oiled heatproof work surface, and sprinkle with the citric acid.

title: Cookbook:Acid Drops
text: Use a greased spatula to fold in the sides and thoroughly work the acid in.

title: Cookbook:Acid Drops
text: When the candy is cool enough to touch but still pliable, roll it into sticks and snip off drop-sized bits.

title: Cookbook:Acid Drops
text: Sift powdered sugar onto the candies, and shake to coat.

title: Cookbook:Acid Drops
text: Allow to cool and harden completely.

title: Cookbook:Acid Drops
text: Store in an air-tight container.

title: Cookbook:Bacon and Egg Pie
text: Preheat the oven to 190°C (370°F or gas mark 5)

title: Cookbook:Bacon and Egg Pie
text: Divide the pastry into two equal portions, roll it out, and line a 20 cm (8-inch) oven-proof dish with one portion.

title: Cookbook:Bacon and Egg Pie
text: Combine the bacon and eggs, then mix in any seasoning or herbs.

title: Cookbook:Bacon and Egg Pie
text: Pour the egg mixture into the lined dish.

title: Cookbook:Bacon and Egg Pie
text: Moisten the edge of the pastry then cover the dish with the second portion of rolled-out pastry.

title: Cookbook:Bacon and Egg Pie
text: Seal the edges.

title: Cookbook:Bacon and Egg Pie
text: Make a small hole in the centre to allow steam to escape.

title: Cookbook:Bacon and Egg Pie
text: If desired, the pastry can be brushed with a beaten egg or milk to improve the browning.

title: Cookbook:Bacon and Egg Pie
text: Bake for about 35–40 minutes in the preheated oven.

title: Cookbook:Banana Caramel Dessert
text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).

title: Cookbook:Banana Caramel Dessert
text: In a small bowl, toss bananas, vanilla, and melted butter until bananas are well coated.

title: Cookbook:Banana Caramel Dessert
text: On a cookie sheet, unroll 2 cinnamon rolls, leaving the two triangles attached to form a square.

title: Cookbook:Banana Caramel Dessert
text: Place ¼ of the banana mixture in the center of each pair of rolls.

title: Cookbook:Banana Caramel Dessert
text: Bake for 11 to 13 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown.

title: Cookbook:Banana Caramel Dessert
text: Heat the caramel topping and drizzle over dessert.

title: Cookbook:Banana Caramel Dessert
text: Serve warm, with ice cream if desired.

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: Put a large heavy frying pan on a hob over a medium heat.

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: Put in a little vegetable oil (if desired) and let it warm up.

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: Then place the sausages in a single layer in the frying pan.

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: Let them fry a minute or so, then turn them over, fry another minute, turn them around again, to try and get a bit of colour all over.

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: Once they've been in the hot pan for 5 minutes or so, turn the heat right down to low.

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: Let them fry very gently for the next 25 minutes, turning them over every 5 or 10 minutes so they get cooked evenly.

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: You can cook them for longer than this (even up to about an hour on a very low heat).

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: Always make sure the sausages are cooked all the way through (no pinkness should remain).

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: Peel the potatoes and chop them roughly into pieces around 1 or 2 cm thick.

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: Add them to a large pan of boiling water and boil vigorously for 15 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: When they're done (they'll be soft enough that you can easily put a knife/fork into one of the pieces), drain them in a colander and return them to the big pan (not on the heat any more).

title: Cookbook:Bangers and Mash
text: Add a generous knob of butter and a splash of milk to the potatoes, and mash them all up with a potato masher.

title: Cookbook:British Christmas Pudding
text: Combine all dried mixed fruit in a large bowl.

title: Cookbook:British Christmas Pudding
text: Stir well.

title: Cookbook:British Christmas Pudding
text: Mix in the flour, then the sugar, lemon, orange, breadcrumbs, and nuts.

title: Cookbook:British Christmas Pudding
text: Whisk eggs in a separate bowl.

title: Cookbook:British Christmas Pudding
text: Mix eggs into the dry ingredients.

title: Cookbook:British Christmas Pudding
text: Steam the pudding for several hours, remove it, and put it in a cool place.

title: Cookbook:British Christmas Pudding
text: Serve with butter, cream, custard, or brandy.

title: Cookbook:Bubble and Squeak
text: Fry the chopped onion in fat or oil.

title: Cookbook:Bubble and Squeak
text: Chop the vegetables, and add to the pan.

title: Cookbook:Bubble and Squeak
text: Cook over a medium heat till the underside is golden brown and crispy, then turn it, scraping the crispy bits into the mix.

title: Cookbook:Bubble and Squeak
text: Repeat the turning and scraping a few times until browned and cooked through.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: Preheat the oven to 180°C (gas mark 4; 350°F).

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: Rub flour, butter, and caster sugar together until it resembles breadcrumbs.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: Press into a 25 x 38 x 4 cm Swiss roll pan.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: Bake for 20 minutes or till golden.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: Cool.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: Melt butter in a heavy-based saucepan over a low heat; add sugar, golden syrup, and condensed milk.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: Stir continuously for 40–50 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: It should be golden brown in colour when ready to eat.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: To test, drop a little blob into a bowl of cold water; it should firm up.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: Pour this caramel mixture over the base, and let it cool.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: Pour melted chocolate over the top.

title: Cookbook:Caramel Squares
text: Spread the chocolate evenly, and let set.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala
text: Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala
text: Add the garlic and onions and stir-fry until browned.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala
text: Add the curry pastes and mix well, adding a little water or yogurt.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala
text: Add the cooked chicken tikka, and stir-fry for two minutes to heat through.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala
text: Add the tomatoes, vinegar, tomato paste, and chilies and simmer for five minutes.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala
text: Add more extra water if needed.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala
text: Add the cream, garam masala, and chopped cilantro and simmer for a few times.

title: Cookbook:Chicken Tikka Masala
text: Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with Naan, rice coloured yellow with turmeric, onion bahjis and/or a glass of white wine.

title: Cookbook:Chip Butty
text: Make sure the chips are not too greasy and have been well drained.

title: Cookbook:Chip Butty
text: Take two slices of bread (the heel works best) and butter both on one side, then apply ketchup and spread evenly over the bread.

title: Cookbook:Chip Butty
text: Add chips in a manner akin to herringbone floor tiling, making sure to minimise any gaps.

title: Cookbook:Chip Butty
text: You can add multiple layers.

title: Cookbook:Chip Butty
text: Put both slices of bread together, then put the assembled sandwich on a flat surface and slap it hard several times with with an open hand to crush the filling.

title: Cookbook:Chip Butty
text: Eat immediately!

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F, GM 6).

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Sift the flour into a bowl.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Rub in the lard and margarine.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Add enough water to bind the mixture into a dough.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Roll out half the dough and use it to line a large flan or quiche dish.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Boil the potatoes.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Drain, add the butter, and mash.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Add the chopped onion and corned beef.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Spoon potato mixture into the lined dish.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Roll out the other half of the pastry mixture.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Lay it over the dish sealing at the edges, forming a lid to the pie.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Cut some slits in the top of the lid.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Brush with a little milk.

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Cook until golden brown (about 35–40 minutes).

title: Cookbook:Corned Beef Pie
text: Serve with vegetables, gravy, chips, peeled plum tomatoes, waffles, anything you like really.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Skin the chicken if needed, and cut it into small pieces.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Traditionally the chicken is cooked whole in advance, but alternatively you can use raw chicken and grill the chicken pieces at this point.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: In a small saucepan, warm a small amount of vegetable oil.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Add the onion to the pan and cook gently until soft (about 3 minutes).

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Add the curry paste, tomato puree, wine, bay leaf and lemon juice.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Simmer uncovered for about 10 minutes until well-reduced.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Strain and leave to cool.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Purée the chopped apricots in a blender or processor.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Beat the cooled sauce into the mayonnaise with the apricot purée.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Whip the cream to stiff peaks, and fold into the mixture.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Season with salt and pepper, and a little lemon juice if necessary.

title: Cookbook:Coronation Chicken
text: Fold in the chicken pieces, garnish with watercress, and serve.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: This method emphasizes broiling and poaching rather than frying.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Heat a broiler to medium heat, and cook the sausages under it, turning frequently.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: They should take about 10–15 minutes total to cook.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Cover the base of a frying pan with about 1cm of water, and heat on a high heat until boiling.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: When it is boiling, carefully break the eggs into it.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: If you have cooking rings, you can put these into the water first and then break the eggs into the rings, to prevent the eggs from spreading too much, although really fresh eggs should stay together anyway.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Once the eggs are in the pan, wait a few moments for the water to heat up again, then turn the heat down to a very very gently simmer.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: To ensure the tops of the eggs are cooked, spoon water from around the edge of the pan over the top of the eggs a few times during cooking.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: When cooked, the egg white should be soft but cooked through and the yolk still runny.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: They should take about 8–10 minutes to cook.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Put the halved tomatoes under the broiler with the sausages.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: They should take about 6 minutes to cook.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: If using, put the baked beans into a saucepan and heat through over a medium heat.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: They should take about 5 minutes to heat through.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Heat up a very small amount of oil in a pan, and fry the mushrooms until they are soft.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: They should take about 4 minutes to cook.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Put the bacon under the grill along with the sausages and tomatoes.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Cook on one side for about 2 minutes, then turn once and repeat.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Cook longer if crispier bacon is preferred.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: This should take about 4 minutes to cook.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Whilst cooking the bacon, toast the bread until golden.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Serve the eggs, bacon, mushrooms, sausage, tomato and beans onto piping hot plates, with the toast on a separate plate or toast rack.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Serve with butter and jam for the toast, and hot tea with milk.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Start toasting the bread before cooking the rest of the food.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Assuming 2 slices per person, you should have enough by the time you finish the fried food.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Be sure to butter them heavily with real butter rather than low-fat spread.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Place 4 plates on the bottom shelf of an oven, and one on the top.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Set the oven to its lowest heat.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Melt some lard in a large frying pan (enough to make a layer of fat around 1 cm deep) and brown the sausage in it over a high heat.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Lower heat and cook the sausage for around 4 minutes, and leave it in the pan.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: A lot of fat will leak from the sausages.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Add the bacon (2 strips per person rather than 1) and cook to taste, flipping regularly (2–3 minutes for pink, 4–6 for a darker red bacon with crispy fat).

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: The bacon will also release a lot of fat.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Add the mushrooms and tomatoes to the pan.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Add the tin of baked beans to a small pot and heat on a separate burner.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: After 2–4 minutes, transfer the mushrooms to the oven with the bacon.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Transfer the tomato then too, or leave it a little longer depending on taste.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: The sausages should now be dark brown, push them to the side of the pan and break an egg into the fat.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Using a spatula, push hot fat over the yolk until it begins to bubble but is still liquid.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: This should take about 1 minute or so in a hot pan.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Set out the 4 warmed plates beforehand and add an egg to each.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: When done, add the sausage, bacon, and mushrooms.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Add the beans last.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Serve with the buttered toast on a separate plate.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: If you are using black pudding, add it to the fat with the bacon and remove it before the eggs.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: If you desire a fried slice, add a slice of bread (whole or cut diagonally, in half or quarters) and allow it to absorb some of the leftover fat and lightly fry, then flip over and repeat.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: Alternatively, you can just fry some bread in vegetable oil in a separate pan but it doesn't have the same flavour as bread fried in the leftover fat from cooking a full breakfast in lard.

title: Cookbook:English Breakfast
text: If a whole slice is used it is preferable to place the fried egg on top, so the yolk runs into the bread and can easily be absorbed by the fried slice.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Preheat the vegetable oil in a deep fryer to 180°C (350°F), or until a cube of bread browns in 15 seconds when added to the oil.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Peel the potatoes and cut into thick wedges.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Deep-fry the potatoes in batches for 6–8 minutes or until they are crisp and golden.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Remove from the oil, and drain on kitchen paper.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Sprinkle with sea salt and keep warm.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: In a bowl, whisk together the plain flour, corn flour, salt, and enough cold water to form a batter.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Cut the fish into thick slices, then coat in the batter.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Deep fry the fish in batches for 5–6 minutes, depending on the size of the fish.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Remove and drain on kitchen paper.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Transfer the fish and chips to serving plates and garnish with lemon wedges and sprig of parsley.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Or for a fun, traditional twist, place the fried fish and chips on brown paper or newsprint.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Top with salt and/or vinegar.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Typically the lemon wedges are squeezed over the fish and the vinegar is sprinkled on the chips.

title: Cookbook:Fish and Chips
text: Also can be served with pickles, pickled onions, tartar sauce, pickled eggs, and mushy peas.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: Sift the flour and salt into a bowl.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: Make a well in the centre.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: Place the water and lard into a saucepan over low heat.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: When the lard has melted, bring to a boil.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: Pour the mixture into the centre of the flour.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: Working very quickly, mix with a wooden spoon.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: Knead briefly with hands to produce a smooth dough.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: Sift the flour and salt into a bowl.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: Place the water and lard into a saucepan over low heat.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: When the lard has melted, bring to a boil.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: Quickly pour the flour into the saucepan.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon.

title: Cookbook:Hot Water Crust Pastry
text: It will form a smooth dough in seconds

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F or Gas Mark 6).

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: Sift the flour into a bowl with the salt.

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: Add the suet and sufficient water to create a soft but not sticky dough.

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: Turn on to a floured board and roll out to a rectangle about 20×30 cm (8×12 inches).

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: Brush the pastry with the warmed jam, leaving a 1 cm (½ inch) border all around.

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: Fold in this border and brush with milk.

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: With the short side towards you, roll up the pastry loosely and seal the ends well.

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: Place on a greased baking sheet, with the sealed edge underneath.

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: Brush with the beaten egg and sprinkle with caster sugar.

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: Bake in the oven for 35–40 minutes until golden brown.

title: Cookbook:Jam Roly-Poly
text: Remove from the oven, sprinkle on a little more sugar and serve hot with home-made English custard.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Cook the rice in one and a half the amount of chicken stock with the bay leaf.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: When it is done and keeping warm, discard the bay leaf, fluff the rice with chopsticks, and place the raw smoked haddock slab on top.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Close the lid and let the haddock steam on warm for 15 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Remove the haddock, and flake with forks to get rid of every last trace of bone.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Place the haddock back with the rice.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Sauté the shallots in excess butter until light brown.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Add the garlic, and cook for 1 minute more, making sure to not brown it.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Transfer mixture to the rice.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Add the eggs, mustard, parsley, pepper, curry powder, and enough cream to make everything just slightly creamy.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Mix it all up, gently and thoroughly (chopsticks are perfect for this).

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Season with salt to taste.

title: Cookbook:Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
text: Serve immediately or later—it keeps well.

title: Cookbook:Lady Arundel's Manchet
text: Mix the salt into the flour, then rub in the butter

title: Cookbook:Lady Arundel's Manchet
text: Combine the yeast with the sugar.

title: Cookbook:Lady Arundel's Manchet
text: Add it to 1½ cups of the warm milk.

title: Cookbook:Lady Arundel's Manchet
text: Beat the egg, and mix with the yeast and flour.

title: Cookbook:Lady Arundel's Manchet
text: Make a well in the flour, pour in the yeast mixture, and mix into a dough.

title: Cookbook:Lady Arundel's Manchet
text: Shape the dough into small, flat, round cakes about ¾ inch thick and 3 ½ inches across.

title: Cookbook:Lady Arundel's Manchet
text: Mark manchets with lines to form a diamond pattern.

title: Cookbook:Lady Arundel's Manchet
text: Leave to rise for 30 minutes in a warm place.

title: Cookbook:Lady Arundel's Manchet
text: Bake in a moderate oven (350-375 °F / 180-190 °C) until cooked.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Put all the ingredients in a wok (a wok is perfect though not traditional) or another large pan.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Add water until almost covering the ingredients.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Cover and bring to boil.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Lower heat, and simmer for 30 minutes or until the potatoes soften.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: If too wet, strain off some water.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Add the broken-up corned beef and stir in gently.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Bring almost to the boil.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Switch off the heat and let it sit for 15 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Heat again or serve as it is.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: It's easy to make hash in a pressure cooker—just follow the pressure cooker instructions to cook the potatoes and onions on the stovetop.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Put all the ingredients except the corned beef into the pressure cooker.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: You do not need much water—perhaps 1–2 cm.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Bring the pressure cooker up to pressure and cook for about 4 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Meanwhile, chop up the corned beef.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: When the other ingredients are cooked, open the pressure cooker and mix in the corned beef.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
text: Serve.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Hotpot
text: Dice the lamb and set aside.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Hotpot
text: Preheat oven to 325°F / 170°C / Gas mark 3.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Hotpot
text: Add a layer of the potatoes to the bottom of a casserole dish, and cover with a handful of the diced onion.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Hotpot
text: Layer the diced lamb on top of this, sprinkling with the herbs.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Hotpot
text: Repeat these layers until the dish is full.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Hotpot
text: Top with a final layer of the potatoes.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Hotpot
text: Pour boiling water into the dish until filled—if more water is needed, continue to add until topped.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Hotpot
text: Bake for at least 1 hour, though traditionally the dish was left baking all day.

title: Cookbook:Lancashire Hotpot
text: Mutton will require a longer cooking time.

title: Cookbook:Lentil, Barley, and Tomato Soup
text: Soak the lentils and barley together overnight, then drain.

title: Cookbook:Lentil, Barley, and Tomato Soup
text: Fry the onion in the butter until soft.

title: Cookbook:Lentil, Barley, and Tomato Soup
text: Add the lentils, barley, and water.

title: Cookbook:Lentil, Barley, and Tomato Soup
text: Cook until the lentils are tender—this will take longer if grains are not soaked.

title: Cookbook:Lentil, Barley, and Tomato Soup
text: Add the tomatoes when the soup is almost ready.

title: Cookbook:Lentil, Barley, and Tomato Soup
text: Purée with a food mill, blender, or food processor.

title: Cookbook:Lentil, Barley, and Tomato Soup
text: Reheat and adjust the seasoning.

title: Cookbook:Liverpool Lamb and Vegetable Soup (Scouse)
text: This is a traditional recipe for Liverpool scouse, also known as "lobscouse".

title: Cookbook:Liverpool Lamb and Vegetable Soup (Scouse)
text: The sauce is not thickened, and it is usual to serve with preserved beetroot or red cabbage and white bread with butter.

title: Cookbook:Liverpool Lamb and Vegetable Soup (Scouse)
text: An even more impoverished variety of this dish is 'blind Scouse', which features no meat.

title: Cookbook:Liverpool Lamb and Vegetable Soup (Scouse)
text: Remove the meat from the bone (if needed), and dice it.

title: Cookbook:Liverpool Lamb and Vegetable Soup (Scouse)
text: Heat a little oil in a large saucepan.

title: Cookbook:Liverpool Lamb and Vegetable Soup (Scouse)
text: Add the meat, and brown it.

title: Cookbook:Liverpool Lamb and Vegetable Soup (Scouse)
text: Add the chopped onions, carrots, and water or meat stock, and as many potatoes as possible.

title: Cookbook:Liverpool Lamb and Vegetable Soup (Scouse)
text: Simmer until everything is cooked.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Mincemeat Tarts are large (8 inch (20cm) diameter or more) open pastry tarts, sometimes with a lattice pastry top, and occasionally also containing baked or stewed apple.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: The smaller pastry topped tarts traditionally served at Christmas are known as Mince Pies.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Wash and dry currants.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Set aside.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Put citron, orange peel, lemon rind, raisins, apples, and suet through a meat grinder using the coarse grinder blade.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Mix in the currants, brandy, and spices.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Store in a tightly-covered plastic container in the refrigerator (do not freeze) for up to 1 year.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Let the pastry warm slightly to almost room temperature.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Place on a floured cutting board and roll it out as necessary.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Use a doughnut cutter with the center removed or a 2½ inch round cookie cutter to cut out tart shells.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Gently press into 1½-inch (4 cm) tart pans.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Fill shells with mincemeat and top with a 1-inch (2.5 cm) round piece of pastry cut with the doughnut hole cutter.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: For added decoration, cut or press a design into the 1 inch pastry round before placing in the center of the filled tart.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Lightly brush the pastry lids with milk, or a mixture of milk and beaten egg.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Bake at 425 °F (220 °C) for approximately 20 minutes or until pastry is lightly browned at the edges.

title: Cookbook:Mincemeat Tart
text: Allow to cool on a wire rack, and dust with icing sugar.

title: Cookbook:Mushy Peas
text: Mushy peas is a popular and characteristic British dish that has helped to give British cooking its well-deserved reputation.

title: Cookbook:Mushy Peas
text: Mushy peas are often served with fish and chips.

title: Cookbook:Mushy Peas
text: Place the peas in 2–3 times their volume of water, along with the baking soda, which speeds the soaking process.

title: Cookbook:Mushy Peas
text: Leave to soak overnight.

title: Cookbook:Mushy Peas
text: The next day, drain the peas, and place in a saucepan with enough water to just cover them.

title: Cookbook:Mushy Peas
text: Add the sugar.

title: Cookbook:Mushy Peas
text: Bring to the boil and simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally to help break up the peas.

title: Cookbook:Mushy Peas
text: Add water or reduce to the desired consistency.

title: Cookbook:Mushy Peas
text: Season to taste with salt and pepper.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: An oatcake is a type of pancake made from oatmeal, cooked on a griddle.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: North Staffordshire oatcakes are a local delicacy in the North Staffordshire (Stoke-on-Trent) area of England, and so may be known to non-locals as a North Staffordshire oatcake or Potteries oatcake.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: These use flour and yeast, whereas other oatcakes do not.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: When pre-cooked, they are a form of fast food, and catering outlets in the area usually offer oatcakes with fillings such as cheese, bacon, sausage and egg.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: They can be re-heated by frying in butter, or by grilling.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: In addition, pikelets are often served alongside oatcakes in a similar fashion.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: Add the salt to the flour and oatmeal.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: Dissolve the yeast with a little warm liquid and add the sugar.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: Allow the mixture to become frothy.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: Mix the dry ingredients with the yeast liquid to make a batter.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: Cover the batter with a clean cloth and leave it in a warm place for an hour.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: Cook the oatcakes on a well-greased griddle.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: Put enough batter onto the griddle to produce an oatcake about 8–9 inches in diameter.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: The surface will be covered in holes as it cooks.

title: Cookbook:North Staffordshire Oatcakes
text: Flip the oatcake after 2–3 minutes when the upper side appears dry and the underneath is golden brown, and cook for another 2–3 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Pastry for Cornish Pasties
text: Combine the dry ingredients, then gradually mix in enough water to make a stiff dough.

title: Cookbook:Pastry for Cornish Pasties
text: Roll dough to about a ¼ inch thick.

title: Cookbook:Pastry for Cornish Pasties
text: Cut out rounds with a tea plate—or other round object about 6in across.

title: Cookbook:Pastry for Cornish Pasties
text: Lay rounds on a pastry-board with half the round propped on a rolling-pin.

title: Cookbook:Pastry for Cornish Pasties
text: Add the filling, and fold dough over filling.

title: Cookbook:Pastry for Cornish Pasties
text: Dampen the edges with water, and press to seal.

title: Cookbook:Pastry for Cornish Pasties
text: Crimp the edges, then make slit in middle of each pasty.

title: Cookbook:Pastry for Cornish Pasties
text: Place on baking sheet, bake in hot oven (450 °F) until golden-brown.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Pease pudding, sometimes known as pease pottage or pease porridge, is a simmered pea preparation, which mainly consists of split yellow or carlin peas, water, salt and spices, often cooked with a bacon or ham joint.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: It is similar in texture to hummus (but harder to cut), light yellow in colour, with a mild taste.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Pease pudding was traditionally produced in England, especially in the industrial Northern areas, though it is now widely available, often in butcher's shops (due to the bacon connection).

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: It is often served with ham and stottie cakes.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Put the ham hock in a pressure cooker and cover with water.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: With the lid on bring to the boil (full pressure).

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Lower the heat and simmer for 30–40 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Remove from the heat and release the pressure.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Take out the hock and put to one side.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Add the split peas.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: With the lid on, bring back to the boil.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Again lower the heat to a simmer (as low as possible).

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Simmer for 25–30 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Remove from the heat and release the pressure.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Put the contents into a bowl with the butter, and mix with a balloon type whisk.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Leave to cool.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Serve on white bread or stottie cake, alone or with ham from the hock.

title: Cookbook:Pease Pudding
text: Refrigerate when cool.

title: Cookbook:Potato Pudding
text: Run the potatoes through a sieve, potato ricer, or mouli-mill.

title: Cookbook:Potato Pudding
text: Gently heat butter and cream together until butter is melted.

title: Cookbook:Potato Pudding
text: Mix into potatoes.

title: Cookbook:Potato Pudding
text: Beat eggs lightly, then mix into potatoes.

title: Cookbook:Potato Pudding
text: Mix in the sugar, currants, lemon zest, nutmeg, and brandy.

title: Cookbook:Potato Pudding
text: Either transfer to pastry-lined dish and bake in a moderately hot oven until golden-brown OR steam in a mould for about an hour.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Queen of puddings is a favourite English bread pudding served with an apricot glaze and a soft meringue topping.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Heat the milk, sugar, lemon zest and butter until just below the boil.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Pour onto the bread crumbs and allow the whole to cool slightly, about 10 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Beat the egg yolks and stir into the bread crumb and milk mixture.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 35 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Remove from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Spread the top with the warmed jam, being careful not to break the surface of the pudding.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Whip the egg whites with the vanilla sugar and a few drops of lemon juice until the mixture reaches soft peaks.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Spread the meringue over the top of the pudding.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Return to the oven and bake for 15 minutes until the meringue has browned.

title: Cookbook:Queen of Puddings
text: Serve as is or with crème anglaise.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Rhubarb crumble is a traditional British dessert.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Served traditionally with custard (though you can of course serve with cream or ice cream) it is a hearty, filling, and warm feast, best served after a light meal.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: This version has a flour-based crumble topping, it and simply uses rhubarb and sugar as the filling (unlike the cornstarch etc. in other versions).

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: The rhubarb juice acts as a sufficient sauce.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Rinse and drain the rhubarb pieces, and place them in a deep ovenproof dish.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Add the light brown sugar and mix briefly.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Put the flours in a mixing bowl.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Add the butter.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: With your fingers (not the palms of your hands), rub the butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Sprinkle the sugar and cinnamon over this mixture, and mix them in briefly.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Sprinkle the crumble mixture over the fruit, making a complete layer.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Do not press the topping down—you want it light and crumbly.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Put the dish in the oven (no lid) for 35–45 minutes until crisp and a bit brown.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble I
text: Serve with custard.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble III
text: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F / gas mark 5).

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble III
text: Cut the rhubarb into pieces and stew for a short time with the caster sugar and water until tender.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble III
text: While the rhubarb is stewing, combine the flour and butter in a bowl until it resembles fine breadcrumbs.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble III
text: Stir in the brown sugar.

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble III
text: Place the cooked rhubarb in a deep pie dish (1 L / 2 pt).

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble III
text: Spoon over the crumble topping and spread out evenly

title: Cookbook:Rhubarb Crumble III
text: Bake crumble for about 25 mins until the crumble is golden brown.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Roast beef, or a roast dinner, is a traditional and classic meal across Britain, the Commonwealth, and Ireland, with the focus on some form of roasted meat, vegetables, gravy, and Yorkshire puddings.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Roast dinners are traditionally served on Sunday, but can also be eaten throughout the week.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: The precise recipe of a roast dinner will vary considerably from person to person, so below is a broad overview of common elements that can be adapted and made your own.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: On the morning of cooking, get the beef joint out of the fridge, and let it stand to warm up to room temperature.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and place a roasting tin in the oven to heat up.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: If you have a spare one, place another onion in the tin as it heats up.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Try and use a cast-iron roasting tin since it conducts heat better.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Combine some plain flour, a little rock-salt and a good pinch of ground pepper. 'Dust' the fatty edges of the joint with the mixture, moistening the fat first by wiping it with a damp cloth, so the flour sticks better.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: In a large frying pan, heat some olive oil, then sear (i.e. briefly fry) the fatty edges of the meat until they are a dark brown colour.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: You may need to hold the joint with a fork whilst you do this to ensure an 'all over tan'.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: It is a good idea, at this point, to brown the surface of the meat itself.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: This will trigger Maillard reactions (browning of sugars and amino acids), giving the meat a brown colour, and improving the flavour immensely.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: At the same time add the spare bones to the frying pan, and make sure these are also well browned.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Remove joint and bones from the frying pan.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Lower the heat, add the red wine to the frying pan, and deglaze it well.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Be careful as the wine might catch on fire!

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Using the spare beef bones, make a 'bed' for the joint on the bottom of the hot roasting tin, adding a coarsely chopped onion to the bed.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: The idea is to keep the joint a little raised from the bottom of the tin.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: It does not need to sit in the cooking juices.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Add a cupful of water and pour the contents of the deglazed frying pan, including the onion, over the joint.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Place the joint on its bed, or on the rack, and put near the top shelf of the oven.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Leave the meat to cook, without opening the oven for about 15 minutes at 200°C (400°F).

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Open the oven and baste the joint.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Reduce the oven temperature to about 180°C (350°F).

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: You no longer need to baste the joint now.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Depending on the way you like your beef, leave the joint in the oven for the following time:

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Rare: 15 minutes per pound (~450g)

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Medium: 20 minutes per pound (~450g)

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Well-done: 25 minutes per pound (~450g)

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Once the cooking has completed, take the joint out of the roasting tin and place it on its own separate dish.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Cover the joint loosely with lots of tin-foil, and leave it to rest for about 15 minutes in a warm part of the kitchen.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: If the joint can be stood up, sprinkle a very little rock salt over the top to enhance the taste.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Place the roasting dish on the stove (if need be light 2 rings, one for either end) and allow the juice to heat up a little.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Add the red wine to the dish, and thoroughly deglaze the dish on a high heat.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: This will also evaporate the alcohol from the wine.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Add a little water (if you are cooking vegetables, add a little of their water) and the Worcestershire sauce.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Bring to a low boil.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Stir in the red jam, mustard, and nutmeg.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: If you are really feeling naughty, you can add some crème fraîche!

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Continue to heat everything on the stove, adding water (or cream or more red wine) until the gravy begins to thicken just a little.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Carefully sieve the lot, reserving the gravy in a bowl.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Peel the potatoes, and trim them so that they are (more or less) the same size.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Retain the peelings.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Put the potatoes into a large saucepan of boiling salted water with a little olive oil.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: If you can, place the peelings in a muslin or cheesecloth sack and add to the boiling water to give the potatoes a little more taste (thanks to Heston Blumenthal for this brilliant idea).

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: While you are doing this, heat the goose fat in a large metal oven-safe frying pan.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Boil the potatoes for 5 minutes only—no more.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Take them off the heat, drain them, and return them to the saucepan dry.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Immediately add the flour to the saucepan and cover with a well-fitting lid.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Holding the lid in place, violently shake the saucepan for about 15 seconds.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: The purpose of this dramatic action is to coat the potatoes with the flour and produce a rough and slightly spiky exterior to the potatoes.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: This will help them roast better and yield a crispy exterior.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Using a large metal spoon, lift the potatoes one-by-one out of the saucepan, and place them in the pan of hot goose fat.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: When they have all been in the frying pan, drain the oil from the pan, and separate the potatoes a little, or move them carefully onto a rack above a roasting dish in the oven.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Don't place them flat onto a roasting dish or they will tend to become soggy.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: There should be a gap of about 1 inch (2.5cm) between each potato.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: This is vital to let air to circulate thus enabling them to become crispy.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Bake the potatoes in the oven with the beef.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: The temperature of the oven really depends on what stage the roast beef is at, about 180°C (350°F).

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: They will take about 30–40 minutes to cook and they should have a golden brown crust.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: About twice during the cooking process, take out the tray of potatoes, and with a fork, gently turn them through 90 or so degrees so they become cooked all over.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: This is not as easy as it sounds, as the potatoes may have formed a crust, so work carefully.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: When finished, they will be crispy on the outside, and delightfully fluffy on the inside.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: The potatoes will produce steam, so when you are ready to serve them, try and find a serving dish where the potatoes can be laid out next to each other, rather than piled upon each other.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: This will stop any steam they produce from making them soggy.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Sometimes, laying them around the beef joint will serve the purpose.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Carve thin slices of the meat.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Serve with the roast potatoes, as well as 3 or more side vegetables such as roast parsnips, green beans, and cabbage with a little bacon.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Don't forget some good quality (or better still home made) creamed horseradish sauce, and Coleman's mustard.

title: Cookbook:Roast Beef
text: Yorkshire pudding also goes very well with this dish.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Add 1 pinch of salt and 1 pinch of mustard powder to the flour.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Mix together the suet and flour with enough water to make a doughy consistency.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Cut the pastry into two portions one slightly larger than the other.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Roll out the larger portion and use it to line a small buttered pie dish.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Finely dice the onion.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Mix together the sausagemeat, diced onion, a pinch of thyme, and plenty of black pepper.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Mash the mixture into the pie dish making sure there are no voids.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Wet the edge of the pastry where it covers the lip of the pie dish.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Roll out the remaining pastry and cover the pie.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Lightly crimp the edge with your thumb and trim.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Cut a hole in the top centre of the pie to allow steam to escape.

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Bake in the oven at 180°C until golden brown on top (30–40 minutes).

title: Cookbook:Sausagemeat Pie
text: Serve with a little gravy poured over the top.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Sponge cake is the most commonly-recognised variety of baked confectionery in Britain.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: It has a sweet taste, often flavoured with vanilla, chocolate or other additions.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: It can be cut and displayed in a very large number of different ways.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Preheat an oven to 400°F.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Cream together the sugar and butter in the mixing bowl.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: They should achieve a creamy texture with quite a thick consistency.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: The longer and faster the butter and sugar are creamed the lighter the cake will be when cooked.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Add both eggs and mix well.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Add all the flour using a fine sieve from a height, adding air to the flour, and beat with wooden spoon in a circular motion, trying to incorporate as much air as possible.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Add any food coloring, flavoring etc. at this point.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: If you add liquid ingredients, add the same volume again of sugar-and-flour mix to compensate.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: If adding dry ingredients, ensure to use equal parts less flour than any extra ingredient added.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Grease 1–2 cake pan(s) with butter.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: You may wish to use a springform pan for this recipe.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Scrape the batter into the pan(s).

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: If using two pans, try to ensure that both tins have an equal amount of batter in them and that both are not more than ¾ filled.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Put the cake tins into the oven and leave them for approximately 10 minutes before checking them.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: The cooking time should eventually reach around 15 minutes: keep checking them regularly after about 8 minutes since ovens vary.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Turn the cake out onto a wire rack to cool.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: If assembling 2 layers of cake, turn one of them upside down and spread the jam or buttercream onto its base.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Stick the other cake top-side up onto the upside-down cake.

title: Cookbook:Sponge Cake I
text: Dust the cake with icing sugar using a fine sieve.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Cut the beef into cubes about 2.5 cm (1 in) square.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Heat oil in a saucepan and fry the onion, without letting it colour.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Add beef, making sure the meat is at room temperature first, and cook until medium brown.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Stir in the flour and cook until dark brown (about 1 minute)

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Add Worcestershire sauce, thyme, marjoram, mustard, bay leaf and seasoning.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Slowly add beef stock and ale, then bring to the boil.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Simmer gently until beef is almost tender, approximately 1 ½ hours.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F).

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Remove meat from heat, skim off any fat, adjust seasoning and add fresh chopped parsley.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Place in pie dish or individual dishes.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Cover pie dish (or dishes) with the pastry and trim edges.

title: Cookbook:Steak and Ale Pie
text: Bake for 20–25 minutes or until pastry is well-risen and golden brown.

title: Cookbook:Strawberry and Yogurt Eton Mess
text: Eton mess is a dessert of English origin consisting of a mixture of strawberries, pieces of meringue and cream, which is traditionally served at Eton College's annual prize-giving celebration picnic on the "Fourth of June" (actually celebrated on the last Wednesday in May).

title: Cookbook:Strawberry and Yogurt Eton Mess
text: Rinse the strawberries, remove the tops, and cut into halves.

title: Cookbook:Strawberry and Yogurt Eton Mess
text: Break the meringues into pieces (not too small) and place into a bowl.

title: Cookbook:Strawberry and Yogurt Eton Mess
text: Put the double cream, vanilla essence, and icing sugar into a bowl.

title: Cookbook:Strawberry and Yogurt Eton Mess
text: Whip until reasonably stiff.

title: Cookbook:Strawberry and Yogurt Eton Mess
text: Combine the whipped cream, yoghurt, strawberries, and meringue, being careful not to mash the meringue into pieces that are too small.

title: Cookbook:Strawberry and Yogurt Eton Mess
text: Serve in bowls.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: Toad in the hole is a baked Yorkshire pudding or thick pastry round, with sausages or pieces of meat in it.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: This recipe is for a sausage toad.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: A further variation is made using fine chopped potatoes in a pudding-basin with a lump of meat in the centre, and then boiling or steaming.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: Bake the sausages with the oil in a roasting pan for 10 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: This cooks the sausages and allows the pan to heat up.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: Add batter to the hot pan.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: The oil should sizzle as the cold batter is added to the pan.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: Bake in the oven for about 40–45 minutes.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: The oven door must not be opened while the batter is baking; once the crust has risen and browned, you can open the oven.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: The outside should be crispy and the inside should be firm.

title: Cookbook:Toad in the Hole
text: Remove and serve hot.

title: Cookbook:Trifle
text: Slice the Swiss roll approximately ¾-inch (2 cm) thick, and line the base of a Pyrex casserole dish with it.

title: Cookbook:Trifle
text: Pour sherry over the swiss roll.

title: Cookbook:Trifle
text: Drain the peaches, keeping the juice/syrup aside and then arrange the peaches over the swiss roll.

title: Cookbook:Trifle

title: Cookbook:Yorkshire Pudding

title: Kochbuch/ Bentheimer Moppen
text: Mehl mit dem Kümmel mischen, Zucker, Eier und geschmolzene Butter dazugeben, alles zu einem Knetteig verarbeiten.

title: Kochbuch/ Bentheimer Moppen
text: Es ist normal, dass der Teig relativ fettig ist.

title: Kochbuch/ Bentheimer Moppen
text: Den Teig zu einer etwa 5 cm durchmessenden Wurst ausrollen und diese in den Kühlschrank geben.

title: Kochbuch/ Bentheimer Moppen
text: Dann dünne Scheiben von der Rolle abschneiden, und diese bei 175° Celsius ca. 10 min, bis die Plätzchen goldbraun sind backen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bentheimer Moppen
text: Achtung: nicht zu lange backen, da der Kümmel sonst bitter wird.

title: Kochbuch/ Berliner Pfannkuchen
text: Das Mehl mit der Hälfte der Milch, dem Zucker und der verflüssigten Butter (nicht wärmer als 35 °C) gleichmäßig vermengen.

title: Kochbuch/ Berliner Pfannkuchen
text: In der anderen Hälfte der Milch die Hefe auflösen, das Salz und die geriebene Zitronenschale hinzugeben.

title: Kochbuch/ Berliner Pfannkuchen
text: Beides zusammenführen und daraus einen glatten Teig kneten, der für rund fünfzehn Pfannkuchen reichen wird.

title: Kochbuch/ Berliner Pfannkuchen
text: Rührmaschinen sind nur bedingt geeignet, der Teig sollte mit der Hand mindestens 10 Minuten durchgeknetet werden - je mehr Arbeit in diesen Schritt gesteckt wird, desto besser wird der Pfannkuchen später aufgehen.

title: Kochbuch/ Berliner Pfannkuchen
text: Den resultierenden Teig zu einer Kugel formen und eine Stunde gehen lassen.

title: Kochbuch/ Berliner Pfannkuchen
text: Hernach auf ungefähr einen halben Zentimeter Dicke ausrollen, kleine Häufchen Pflaumenmus mit einem Teelöffel heraufgeben und mit einer zweiten gleich dicken Teigschicht bedecken.

title: Kochbuch/ Berliner Pfannkuchen
text: Nun um die Pflaumenmushaufen herum rund ausstechen (Ausstechform oder Glas verwenden).

title: Kochbuch/ Berliner Pfannkuchen
text: Die resultierenden Pfannkuchen-Rohlinge etwa zwei Stunden auf Backpapier gehen lassen, bis sich etwa faustgroße Pfannkuchen-Rohlinge gebildet haben. (Dies nach Möglichkeit nicht auf der Heizung oder im Backofen, denn je wärmer der Teig während der Gehzeit wird, desto leichter fällt er anschließend wieder in sich zusammen.) Anschließend Fett (Kokosfett oder Schweineschmalz) zusammen mit einer Vanilleschote bis zum Sieden erhitzen.

title: Kochbuch/ Berliner Pfannkuchen
text: Mit kleineren Teigresten testen, ob das Fett heiß genug ist (der Teig muss direkt nach dem Hereingeben oben schwimmen und in weniger als einer halben Minute braun werden).

title: Kochbuch/ Berliner Pfannkuchen
text: So dies der Fall ist, die Pfannkuchen gleichmäßig von beiden Seiten darin dunkelbraun ausbacken und nach dem Abkühlen mit Puderzucker bestreuen.

title: Kochbuch/ Birnen, Bohnen und Speck
text: Man koche den Speck mit der zerhackten Zwiebel im Wasser 20 Minuten.

title: Kochbuch/ Birnen, Bohnen und Speck
text: Währenddessen kann man die Bohnschoten vorbereiten, indem man sie putzt, wäscht, und ev. in mundgerechte Stücke bricht.

title: Kochbuch/ Birnen, Bohnen und Speck
text: Die Birnen lasse man ganz, einschließlich dem Stiel, um sie am Zerfallen zu hindern; einzig die Blütenreste entferne man

title: Kochbuch/ Birnen, Bohnen und Speck
text: Dann gebe man die Bohnschoten und das Bohnenkraut hinzu und koche den Eintopf weitere 15 Minuten

title: Kochbuch/ Birnen, Bohnen und Speck
text: Schließlich lege man die Birnen auf/in den Eintopf; sie müssen nicht völlig eingetaucht sein; und koche den Eintopf weitere 15 Minuten

title: Kochbuch/ Birnen, Bohnen und Speck
text: Kurz vor dem Servieren versprudle man das Mehl mit etwas Wasser oder der Eintopfflüssigkeit, rühre dies in den Eintopf, den man dann durch neuerliches Aufkochen bindet.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Kartoffeln schälen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: In ca. 2 cm große Würfel oder höchstens 0,5 cm dicke Scheiben schneiden.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Kartoffelstücke waschen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Kartoffeln grob in dicke Scheiben schneiden.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Bratfett in die heiße Pfanne geben.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Die Kartoffeln ggf. zusammen mit dem Kümmel in die Pfanne geben und ca. 10 Minuten braten, dabei wenden.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Wichtig: Die Kartoffelscheiben sollten nebeneinander und nicht übereinander liegen, um gleichmäßig durchbraten zu können!

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Daher größere Mengen ggf. in mehreren Durchgängen verarbeiten.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Bei rohen Kartoffeln die Pfanne für ca. 10 Min. abdecken, danach offen weiterbraten.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Bei rohen Kartoffeln mit einer Messerspitze hineinstechen um den Gargrad festzustellen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Eventuell noch mehr Fett dazugeben, wenn die Kartoffeln viel aufnehmen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Wenn die Kartoffeln fast gar sind die Zwiebeln hinzugeben und darauf achten dass diese nicht schwarz werden

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Wenn die Kartoffeln an allen Seiten goldbraun sind, sind sie gar.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Erst jetzt salzen und pfeffern.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Falls gewünscht, Speck und frische Kräuter (z.B. Majoran oder Petersilie) hinzugeben.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Zwei Eier in eine Tasse schlagen und mit einer Gabel Eiweiß und Eigelb vermischen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bratkartoffeln
text: Die Eier in der noch heißen Pfanne unter die Bratkartoffeln heben.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Weiße Bohnen über Nacht einweichen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Am nächsten Tag mit dem Einweichwasser zum Kochen bringen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Schweinebauch hineingeben.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Salzen. 60 Minuten kochen lassen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Möhren, Lauch und Zwiebel putzen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Waschen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: In kleine Würfel (Lauch in Streifen ) schneiden.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Auch hineingeben.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Noch 30 Minuten kochen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: In der Zwischenzeit die grünen Bohnen waschen, fädeln und kleinschneiden.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Kartoffeln schälen und würfeln.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Beides 25 Minuten mitkochen lassen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Fleisch rausnehmen.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: In Streifen schneiden.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Wieder hineingeben.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Mit Salz, Pfeffer und Streuwürze abschmecken.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Gewaschene Petersilie hacken.

title: Kochbuch/ Bremer bunte Finken
text: Vor dem Servieren darüberstreuen.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Pancakes in der beschichteten Pfanne backen und drehen, wenn die Bläschen platzen.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Die Eier mit dem Salz, ggf. dem Staubzucker (Puderzucker) und ungefähr der Hälfte der Milch versprudeln oder verrühren.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Keinen Zucker nimmt man, wenn man die Palatschinken zur Suppeneinlage „Frittaten“ weiterverarbeitet, Zuckerzusatz bewirkt, dass der Teig beim Herausbacken besser bräunt.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Anschließend das Mehl nach und nach zugeben, und solange rühren, bis keine Klumpen mehr im Teig sind.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Den Rest der Milch und ggf. das Mineralwasser langsam einarbeiten, bis der Teig die Konsistenz wie flüssiges Obers (Sahne) hat.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Je dünner der Teig, desto dünner werden die Palatschinken.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Dann den Teig ca. 30 Minuten „gehen“ lassen, damit das Mehl quellen kann.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Sollte der Teig nach dem Quellen zu dünn sein und in der Palatschinke Löcher oder Poren entstehen, kann man den Teig einfach mit Mehl eindicken ohne ihn erneut „gehen“ zu lassen.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Fett in die Pfanne geben

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: entweder als haselnussgroßes Stück Butter(schmalz) und schmelzen lassen

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: oder einen Kaffeelöffel zerlassenes Fett oder Öl

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: oder mithilfe eines Silikon-Backpinsel die Pfanne mit Öl ausstreichen

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: das flüssige Fett in der Pfanne durch Schwenken verteilen (es soll nicht zu heiss werden, also nicht rauchen)

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: einen nicht zu großen Schöpflöffel (Schöpfkelle) voll Teig hineingeben und durch Schwenken/Verrinnen lassen gleichmäßig verteilen.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Solange warten, bis die Oberseite „käsig“ (wie fester Butterkäse) aussieht und dann die Palatschinke wenden.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Dabei etwas Fett zugeben und von der zweiten Seite fertigbacken, so dass beide Seiten hellbraun sind.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Danach die Palatschinke auf einen erwärmten Teller gleiten lassen, mit erwärmter Füllung bestreichen, einrollen oder auf ein Viertel zusammenschlagen, verzieren und paarweise oder einzeln möglichst heiß auftragen.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Die Pfannkuchen und Palatschinken können in zahlreichen Varianten serviert werden.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Nußnugatcreme, Honig, Ahornsirup u.a.m.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: heiße, flüssige Schokolade

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Obst gemischt oder pur, zum Beispiel Heidelbeeren, Kirschen, Erdbeeren, Bananen oder Birnen, heiße Himbeeren,

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Speiseeis, dazu Schlagsahne, Vanille- oder Schokoladensauce.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Rasch servieren!

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: Das Eis darf nicht flüssig werden, der Teig sollte noch warm sein.

title: Kochbuch/ Eierpfannkuchen
text: gehackte und geröstete Nüsse, vor allem geröstete Haselnüsse oder Walnüsse, oder Kokosflocken, vorzugsweise zusammen mit heißer Schokoladensauce /und ev.
